findings.issue: The jsdom mount test asserts the full message text is present in the DOM (screen.getByText) and that the component doesn't throw, but jsdom does not perform real layout/reflow — it cannot verify that `white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word` on .chs-banner__violation-message actually prevents horizontal overflow or a broken banner at 550+ chars in a real viewport. The pr-handoff's phrasing that the mount test 'covers' the pre-wrap layout claim is a bit strong — it covers crash-freedom and text-completeness, not visual layout.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking. The CSS pattern itself (pre-wrap + word-break:break-word, no fixed width/overflow:hidden ancestor) is the textbook-correct fix for this exact failure mode and .chs-banner has no max-height/overflow clip, so risk is low. If wanted, a real-browser (Playwright) screenshot/overflow assertion in a future pass would close this gap; not required to merge.
